summary: Unmatched pits two (or more) wildly asymmetric heroes against each other in dice-free, card-driven combat on a point-to-point map, where every fighter's unique deck defines a completely different playstyle. King Arthur, Merlin, Alice, Sinbad, and Medusa each demand different tactics, so matches feel fresh even after many plays.
praised: high replayability from mixing and matching sets
criticised: four-player free-for-all is less tight than head-to-head duels
a single base set has a smaller matchup pool on its own
some heroes are simpler than others, creating a slight skill ceiling gap

interaction.kind: asymmetric duel on a shared map
interaction.detail: Both heroes and their sidekicks move and fight on one shared point-to-point map, so positioning blocks movement and lines of attack. Combat directly damages and eliminates opposing characters, making the fight itself the entire point of contact between players.

subsystems: combat resolution reducing a hero's health
scoring.how_you_win: On your turn you move, play a scheme card, or attack an adjacent enemy hero with a matching-value card; the game ends the instant the opposing side's hero(es) are all reduced to 0 health, with no further point counting.
scoring.score_note: win by defeating opponent's fighters, no score

_name: Unmatched: Battle of Legends, Volume One
